Use case: precise-object-edit. This exact portrait illustration is the edit target. Keep the ORIGINAL INDUSTRIAL MANIPULATOR, its exact mechanical structure, proportions, pose, size, location, joints, steel/ivory material colors and professional industrial character. Do not redesign it, do not turn it into a toy/cartoon arm, do not replace it with simple smooth plastic segments. Keep the room composition, pegboard, main lamp, timber/steel supports, bench perspective, and portrait crop.
The user only wants LESS VISUAL NOISE and LESS EXCESSIVE REFLECTIVE DETAIL. Make the robot's metal surfaces more matte: remove the dozens of sharp tiny orange reflection specks, dense scratch clusters and high-frequency contrast on its plates. Replace surface glitter with a few broad restrained warm highlights and readable shaded planes. Keep the engineering geometry and meaningful joints/bolts, with calm material shading. Clean up unnecessary loose mini-parts on the tabletop surrounding the machine: remove the scattered little screws and surplus metal boxes, retaining the primary work module, one coherent base, the large draft sheet and one screwdriver. Do not add any new objects.
Maintain the same warm amber/navy illustrated workshop rendering as the input, crisp dark contours and subtle worn texture, but less shiny/noisy. The main machine must remain recognizably the SAME detailed industrial manipulator. No green glow, no neon, no windows or city, no people, no words/UI/cards. Change only surface noise/reflections and loose bench clutter.

In the foreground on the desk stands ONE tan manila project folder, facing the viewer, slightly turned in perspective; upright, not a flat leather portfolio. It has a couple of small brass rivets and the single word CASES clearly printed in black. This folder is the dominant front object, with its lower edge firmly resting on the table. Put the monitor approximately at 25%-49% image height and the folder at 45%-66%. A few flat cream documents are nearby, nothing piled high. Warm wood desk continues through the lower quarter under the separate caption area. Preserve the reference's layered depth, restrained detail and simple material palette.
Text allowed ONLY the exact word CASES on the tan folder. No rocket-engine posters, no city architecture chalk drawing instead of the world map, no brown leather lying folder, no tool container, no cubical terminal objects, no decorative typewriter.
